newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Banpais says auction on track.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Banpais says auction on track.

text.p: The auction of Mexico's intervened Banpais is running on track and could happen by May, a company official said on Monday.

"There is not a definite date for taking the bids," Carlos Peralta, director of investor relations for the bank, told Reuters. "Certainly it will be this year, and the mentioned date of May could be correct."
Banpais has been taken over by the Mexican government because on gross mismanagement charges. Its former president, Angel Rodriguez, was arrested in Spain, and Mexico has requested his extradition.
The Mexico City daily Reforma reported on Monday that the auction would be complete by May and that Rodrguez would be extradited to Mexico within six weeks.
A foreign ministry spokeswoman could not confirm that Rodrguez would be extradited any time soon, but said that the request with Spain was "in process."
Seven foreign and national financial institutions are bidding on the troubled bank.
Of the bidders, five are foreign and two Mexican, Peralta said, but he said he could not identify them because of a confidentiality agreement.
Rothschild Mexico SA de CV and Rothschild Inc are handling the sale.

The management of Grupo Financiero Asemex-Banpais, which once controlled bank Banpais, was taken over by Mexican government regulators in March 1995 due to charges of administrative irregularities. In August 1996, the Mexican bank bailout fund Fobaproa took over all of Banpais's shares, severing its relationship with the financial group.
Peralta said that in determining the concessionaire the price bid at auction would be less important than the business plan offered for turning Banpais around.
The seven bidders were chosen by Fobaproa and the National Bank and Securities Commission (CNBV) from an initial list of 34 institutions invited to bid on Banpais, Peralta said.
Last year, Mexico's Grupo Financiero Banorte said it had begun negotiations with the federal government to buy Banpais.
"Banorte has always been mentioned, but I cannot comment," Peralta said.

The auction of Banpais is commonly referred to as a second privatization. Mexican banks were privatized during the administration of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari (1988-1994). Former President Jos Lpez Portillo (1976-1982) nationalized the banks toward the end of his term.
